notes.compsSubtitle: Sourced EV ($m) and TTM revenue ($m) are historical market inputs; EV / TTM revenue is formula-driven. These are not ARR multiples or forward exit valuations.
interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The observed multiples are EV / historical revenue. Exit valuation assumptions are EV / exit ARR. Revenue and ARR are not automatically equal.
Market prices can change daily, and peer equity valuations include different debt, cash, growth, FCF, dilution and company-specific risk.
notes.inputSource: Input source: S&P Global Market Intelligence data distributed by StockAnalysis (as of Nov 2, 2026); operating context from corporate earnings releases.
notes.reverseTitle: EXIT MULTIPLE REVIEW | LIVE REVERSE UNDERWRITING
notes.reverseSubtitle: No change to approved original underwriting. This sheet tests how today's market EV / TTM revenue observations compare with 2031 modeled EV / ARR assumptions.
reverseNotes: Required EV / ARR holds modeled ARR, ownership, net debt and holding period fixed, then solves for a target 20% gross IRR.
Required 2031 ARR holds the modeled exit multiple fixed, then solves for ARR at the target gross IRR.
The observed peer median is an alternative heuristic, not a forecast or an analytically justified exit multiple.
No multiples have been changed in the original Assumptions, Returns, Valuation Matrix, or website parity baseline.
A rigorous next diligence round needs customer retention, cohort contribution, margins, capital stack, security rights and exit market access.
notes.dealsSubtitle: Equity-financing valuations and M&A prices do not equal public-market EV multiples. Date alignment and security rights matter. No private signal automatically sets our exit multiple.
dealCautions: CAUTION: The Wiz quotient is an upper bound if ARR was greater than $1B; it is not a transaction EV / ARR multiple.
The Chainguard Series D quotient is equity value / ARR at announcement, with unknown capital structure and security preferences.
The Vanta / Chainguard cross-date quotients are deliberately included as an example of a misleading shortcut, not valuation observations.
